report.finding: The negative-feedback term and reaction network are written correctly — nothing structural is wrong, and the CVode settings (tight tolerances, stiff mode) are not damping anything artificially. The decay is a genuine property of the ODE system at these parameter values. For a 3-variable Goodwin oscillator with equal linear decay/production rates (k1=k2=k3=1) as here, the Hill coefficient n has to exceed a critical value (~8, exactly the classic Griffith/Goodwin threshold for a 3-step loop) for the fixed point to lose stability via a Hopf bifurcation and give sustained limit-cycle oscillations. At n=8 you are sitting essentially right at/just below that boundary, so the eigenvalues of the Jacobian at the fixed point have negative real part (a lightly damped oscillatory mode) — hence "a couple of wobbles then flatline," exactly what's plotted. This is expected behaviour of the model as parameterised, not a bug in the feedback term or the integrator.

Raised n to 12 (k1=k2=k3, v0, K unchanged) and reran: amplitude stays large out to t=300 (S1 swinging between ~0.6 and ~5+, no decay), i.e. sustained oscillation, confirming the loop-gain/Hill-exponent threshold is the deciding factor, not solver settings. recommended_changes.why: With k1=k2=k3=1, n=8 sits at/below the Hopf bifurcation threshold for this 3-variable Goodwin loop, so the fixed point is stable and oscillations damp out. Increasing the Hill coefficient (loop gain) above the critical value, e.g. n=12, pushes the system past the bifurcation into sustained limit-cycle oscillation while keeping the same feedback structure.
